discovery: Matter-wave interferometry with atoms and its development into precision inertial and gravitational sensors

nominees.name: Christian J. Bordé
nominees.affiliation: Université Paris 13 / SYRTE, Observatoire de Paris, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Bordé showed that photon recoil in Ramsey-type spectroscopy forms an atom interferometer, and gave its general theory. Pritchard's group made the first interferometer for atoms with nanofabricated gratings and used it for precision measurements of atomic properties. Kasevich, starting with his 1991 light-pulse interferometer with Chu, built it into gravimeters, gyroscopes and gradiometers whose sensitivity rivals or beats classical instruments. These interferometers set the best values of the fine-structure constant and of Newton's G, test the equivalence principle at the 10^-12 level, and are now portable instruments used in geodesy and navigation. Like optical clocks, they treat the quantum phase of atoms as a ruler for gravity and inertia. That opens fundamental physics to precision measurement, including tests of general relativity and searches for dark matter and gravitational waves. The idea is deep, and it took decades of careful work to make it real.
